title: One lease keeper for every leased job, so a hung call cannot keep a job past its lease
description: Worker.encode keeps the lease on the goroutine that does the I/O: the heartbeat, the store puts and most queries share one select loop, and only the ownership check has a deadline (the pool sets no statement timeout, the S3 client uses the SDK's default HTTP client). A query that never answers blocks the loop and the lease check never runs, holding the ffmpeg and the slot. runSubtitle already solves this with a timer that a bounded renewal puts off; lease renewal is written three times with three behaviours (encode, awaitJob, runSubtitle).
acceptanceCriteria: A lease keeper with a connection of its own renews every leased job of the worker, one statement per job table in its own transaction, no keeper statement waits for a row while it holds one, bounded by half a heartbeat, retried at once and then at a short interval when it fails; the transcode loop, awaitJob and runSubtitle use it, and one renewal UPDATE per job table is left in the code

Each job is cut the table's cutMargin (0.5 s) before its lease could lapse, counted from the send of its last confirmed renewal: with the worker's connections held open and unanswered while a job is paused at its lead, its ffmpeg is gone within one lease; with only the pool held and the keeper answering, a job whose work has not come round for a lease is given up, its ffmpeg gone and a replacement serving the next request; a setup copy that is slow but moving counts as work coming round

With every round trip held 1 s (under half a heartbeat), set before the job is claimed, the job goes on and stores every segment; with the keeper's connection alone severed once under that delay, the job goes on; with Postgres away from 2.9 s after a renewal for 3.3 s, every job keeps its row, worker and ffmpeg

No put begins more than a round trip after the job stopped being the worker's, whatever stopped it: a cancel just after a renewal (no put more than 350 ms later), a reap that deletes the row and cuts the lease while the pool is held, a lease held past by a late answer, a worker stopped after the answer; a fence renews only the jobs that asked; the existing fenced-put and outage checks pass

A renewal counts only when confirmed: with the subtitle table's renewal made to fail or block past its bound, the transcode job's lease in Postgres and the keeper's cut agree and the transcode job goes on; under real contention (a worker with two jobs against repeated reaps and cancels, 200 rounds) no request fails and no renewal is lost

The liveness lock's connection refused for longer than a lease while the keeper's and the pool's answer: the worker is not forgotten and the job goes on with the same ffmpeg; the docs state two connections per worker

A Postgres outage that ends 1.5 s before a job's lease can lapse, and a worker stopped until then, cost no job: the same row, worker and ffmpeg, the lease moved on and no job given up (the cut is the lease less the cutMargin, never a heartbeat before it); an outage whose last retry would only come at the next heartbeat still renews by its first retry
notes: Design reviewed by Fable 5.2 (.results/js105-design-review-2026-11-14.md): the keeper's own connection and batched renewal kept; the put fence still asks Postgres, through the keeper, for the asking jobs only.
